What is Fortran and what is it used for?

Fortran (Formula Translation) is the oldest high-level programming language, created in 1957.

Remains dominant in:
- Scientific computing and numerical analysis
- Weather forecasting and climate modeling
- HPC (High Performance Computing)
- Computational physics and chemistry

Modern Fortran (2003/2008/2018) includes OOP, coarrays for parallelism, and interoperability with C.

Tools: **gfortran** (GCC), **ifort** (Intel), **nvfortran** (NVIDIA), **flang** (LLVM).

Write a Hello World in Fortran and show how to compile it.

```fortran
! hello.f90
program hello
    implicit none
    print *, "Hello, World!"
    write(*, '(A)') "Hello, Fortran!"
    write(*, '(A, A, A)') "Hello, ", "modern ", "Fortran!"
end program hello
```

```bash
gfortran hello.f90 -o hello && ./hello
gfortran -O2 -o hello hello.f90   # with optimization
```

- `implicit none` — requires all variables to be declared explicitly (always use this!)
- `print *` — free-format output to stdout
- `write(*, '(fmt)')` — formatted output

What are the intrinsic types in Fortran and how do you declare variables?

```fortran
program types_demo
    implicit none

    ! Integer kinds
    integer :: i            ! default
    integer(kind=4) :: i32  ! 32-bit
    integer(kind=8) :: i64  ! 64-bit

    ! Real kinds
    real :: r               ! single precision (~7 digits)
    real(kind=8) :: d       ! double precision (~15 digits)
    double precision :: dp  ! same as real(8)

    ! Complex
    complex :: z

    ! Logical
    logical :: flag

    ! Character
    character(len=20) :: name

    ! Constants (parameters)
    integer, parameter :: N = 100
    real, parameter :: PI = 3.14159265358979_8  ! _8 = double kind

    ! Assignments
    i = 42
    d = 3.14159265358979d0   ! d0 = double
    z = (3.0, 4.0)           ! real + imaginary
    flag = .true.             ! .TRUE. or .FALSE.
    name = "Alice"
end program types_demo
```

What are the arithmetic and math intrinsic functions in Fortran?

```fortran
print *, 10 / 3          ! 3  (integer division!)
print *, 10.0 / 3.0      ! 3.333...
print *, 10 ** 3         ! 1000
print *, mod(17, 5)      ! 2
print *, abs(-5)         ! 5
print *, sqrt(16.0)      ! 4.0
print *, sin(0.0), cos(0.0)
print *, exp(1.0), log(exp(1.0))
print *, max(3, 7, 2), min(3, 7, 2)
print *, floor(3.7), ceiling(3.2), nint(3.5)

! Type conversion
print *, real(42)        ! 42.0
print *, int(3.7)        ! 3
print *, dble(3.14)      ! 3.14 as double
```

Be careful: `10 / 3` is **integer division** and gives 3. Use `10.0 / 3.0` for floating-point division.

How do arrays work in Fortran? Show declaration, access, slices, and whole-array operations.

```fortran
! 1D array (1-indexed!)
integer, dimension(5) :: arr = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
real :: x(100)

! 2D array
real :: mat(3, 3)

! Access — 1-indexed!
print *, arr(1)      ! 1  (first element)
print *, arr(5)      ! 5  (last element)

! Slices
print *, arr(2:4)    ! 2 3 4
print *, arr(1:5:2)  ! 1 3 5  (stride of 2)
print *, arr(:3)     ! 1 2 3
print *, arr(3:)     ! 3 4 5
print *, arr(::-1)   ! 5 4 3 2 1  (reversed)

! Whole-array operations (vectorized — no loop needed!)
arr = arr * 2        ! multiply every element
arr = arr + 100      ! add to every element

! Implied do loop — fill with values
real :: v(100)
v = [(real(i), i=1,100)]   ! 1.0 to 100.0
```

What are the array intrinsic functions in Fortran?

```fortran
print *, size(arr)           ! total elements
print *, size(mat, 1)        ! size of first dimension
print *, shape(arr)          ! [5]
print *, shape(mat)          ! [3, 3]
print *, lbound(arr, 1)      ! 1  (lower bound)
print *, ubound(arr, 1)      ! 5  (upper bound)
print *, sum(arr)            ! sum of all elements
print *, product(arr)        ! product of all elements
print *, maxval(arr), minval(arr)
print *, maxloc(arr), minloc(arr)  ! index of max/min
print *, dot_product([1,2,3], [4,5,6])  ! 32
print *, matmul(mat, mat)    ! matrix multiply
print *, transpose(mat)      ! transpose

! where — element-wise conditional
x = where(x > 0, x, -x)    ! element-wise abs
```

How do allocatable arrays work in Fortran?

```fortran
! Allocatable 1D array
real, allocatable :: dynamic(:)
allocate(dynamic(100))
dynamic = 0.0
deallocate(dynamic)

! Allocatable 2D array
real, allocatable :: m(:,:)
allocate(m(3, 4))
m = 0.0
m(2, 3) = 42.0
deallocate(m)

! Check if allocated
if (allocated(dynamic)) then
    print *, size(dynamic)
end if
```

Always `deallocate` what you `allocate` to avoid memory leaks. Modern Fortran also supports automatic deallocation when allocatable variables go out of scope.

How does control flow work in Fortran? Show if, do, do while, and select case.

```fortran
! if/else
if (x > 0) then
    print *, "positive"
else if (x < 0) then
    print *, "negative"
else
    print *, "zero"
end if

! Logical operators: .and. .or. .not. .eqv. .neqv.
if (x > 0 .and. x < 10) print *, "small positive"

! do loop
do i = 1, 10
    print *, i
end do

do i = 1, 10, 2   ! step of 2: 1,3,5,7,9
    print *, i
end do

! do while
n = 1
do while (n < 100)
    n = n * 2
end do

! exit and cycle (like break and continue)
do i = 1, 10
    if (mod(i, 2) == 0) cycle  ! skip even
    if (i > 7) exit             ! stop at 7
    print *, i
end do

! select case
select case (i)
    case (1)      ;  print *, "one"
    case (2, 3)   ;  print *, "two or three"
    case (4:10)   ;  print *, "4 to 10"
    case default  ;  print *, "other"
end select
```

How do named loops and nested loop control work in Fortran?

```fortran
! Nested loops with labels
outer: do i = 1, 5
    inner: do j = 1, 5
        if (i * j > 15) exit outer   ! exit the OUTER loop
        if (i == j) cycle inner       ! skip to next j
        print *, i, j
    end do inner
end do outer
```

`exit outer` jumps out of both loops at once. Without the label, `exit` would only exit the innermost loop. This is cleaner than using flag variables to break out of nested loops.

How do subroutines and functions work in Fortran? What are intent attributes?

```fortran
program procedures_demo
    implicit none
    integer :: a=5, b=3, result
    result = factorial(10)
    call swap(a, b)
contains

    ! Subroutine (no return value)
    subroutine swap(x, y)
        implicit none
        integer, intent(inout) :: x, y   ! read AND write
        integer :: temp
        temp = x; x = y; y = temp
    end subroutine swap

    subroutine read_only(name)
        implicit none
        character(len=*), intent(in) :: name  ! read-only
        print *, "Hello, " // trim(name) // "!"
    end subroutine

    ! Function (returns value)
    integer function factorial(n)
        implicit none
        integer, intent(in) :: n
        integer :: i
        factorial = 1
        do i = 2, n
            factorial = factorial * i
        end do
    end function factorial

end program procedures_demo
```

**intent** attributes:
- `intent(in)` — read-only
- `intent(out)` — write-only (must be set before use)
- `intent(inout)` — read-write

How do recursive functions and assumed-shape array arguments work in Fortran?

```fortran
! Recursive function — must declare 'recursive'
recursive integer function fib(n) result(res)
    implicit none
    integer, intent(in) :: n
    if (n <= 1) then
        res = n
    else
        res = fib(n-1) + fib(n-2)
    end if
end function fib

! Assumed-shape array argument — any size
function vec_sum(v) result(s)
    implicit none
    real, intent(in) :: v(:)   ! accepts any 1D array
    real :: s
    s = sum(v)
end function vec_sum

! Function returning an array
function linspace(a, b, n) result(v)
    implicit none
    real, intent(in) :: a, b
    integer, intent(in) :: n
    real :: v(n)
    integer :: i
    do i = 1, n
        v(i) = a + (b - a) * (i - 1) / (n - 1)
    end do
end function linspace
```

How do modules and derived types work in Fortran?

```fortran
module geometry
    implicit none
    private                      ! everything private by default

    real, parameter, public :: PI = 3.14159265358979

    type, public :: Circle
        real :: x, y, radius
    contains
        procedure :: area     => circle_area
        procedure :: print    => circle_print
    end type Circle

contains

    real function circle_area(self)
        class(Circle), intent(in) :: self
        circle_area = PI * self%radius**2
    end function circle_area

    subroutine circle_print(self)
        class(Circle), intent(in) :: self
        print *, "Circle at (", self%x, ",", self%y, ") r=", self%radius
    end subroutine circle_print

end module geometry

! Usage
program use_geometry
    use geometry
    implicit none
    type(Circle) :: c
    c%x = 0.0; c%y = 0.0; c%radius = 5.0
    call c%print()
    print *, "Area:", c%area()
end program use_geometry
```

Use `%` to access derived type members (like `.` in other languages). `class(T)` instead of `type(T)` enables polymorphism.

How does file I/O work in Fortran?

```fortran
! Open a file
open(unit=10, file='data.txt', status='replace', action='write', iostat=ios)
if (ios /= 0) stop "Error opening file"

! Write
write(10, '(A)') "Hello, World!"
write(10, '(I5, F10.4)') 42, 3.14159
close(10)

! Read
open(unit=20, file='data.txt', status='old', action='read')
read(20, '(A)') line
read(20, *) i, x    ! free-format read

! Read until EOF
do
    read(20, *, iostat=ios) x
    if (ios /= 0) exit    ! end of file
    print *, x
end do
close(20)

! Format codes
! I10  — right-justified integer width 10
! F12.4 — float width 12, 4 decimal places
! E15.6 — scientific notation
! A20  — character width 20
```

How do coarrays work for parallel programming in Fortran?

```fortran
! Coarrays — Fortran 2008, built-in parallelism
program coarray_demo
    implicit none
    integer :: n[*]      ! coarray — each image has its own copy
    integer :: me, nimages

    me = this_image()
    nimages = num_images()

    n = me * 10          ! each image sets its own n

    sync all             ! barrier — wait for ALL images

    if (me == 1) then    ! image 1 reads from all
        do i = 1, nimages
            print *, "Image", i, "n =", n[i]
        end do
    end if

    ! Put value to another image
    if (me == 1) n[2] = 999
    sync all

    ! Critical section
    critical
        print *, "Image", me, "in critical section"
    end critical
end program coarray_demo
```

Compile: `gfortran -fcoarray=single coarray.f90` (single image) or `gfortran -fcoarray=lib -lcaf_mpi coarray.f90` (MPI).

How does OpenMP work with Fortran for shared-memory parallelism?

```fortran
program openmp_demo
    use omp_lib
    implicit none
    integer :: tid
    real :: sum_val

    ! Parallel region
    !$omp parallel private(tid)
    tid = omp_get_thread_num()
    print *, "Thread", tid, "of", omp_get_num_threads()
    !$omp end parallel

    ! Parallel do loop with reduction
    sum_val = 0.0
    !$omp parallel do reduction(+:sum_val)
    do i = 1, 1000000
        sum_val = sum_val + real(i)
    end do
    !$omp end parallel do
    print *, "Sum:", sum_val

    ! Parallel sections
    !$omp parallel sections
    !$omp section
    call task_a()
    !$omp section
    call task_b()
    !$omp end parallel sections

end program openmp_demo
```

Compile: `gfortran -fopenmp openmp_demo.f90`. Set threads: `export OMP_NUM_THREADS=4`.
